name: 2 Tone Records
ownershipStory: Founded in Coventry in 1979 by Jerry Dammers of the Specials and financed by Chrysalis, which agreed to fund up to 15 singles a year and release at least 10, leaving the label its own choices. Its contracts let an act leave after a single release, and Madness and the Beat both did. The label stopped operating in 1986; the name survives as a reissue imprint.
hook: A Coventry band's own label, funded by a major, that made Black and white musicians playing together its whole identity.

blurb.age13: Jerry Dammers of the Specials started 2 Tone Records in Coventry in 1979. A bigger company, Chrysalis, paid for the records but let 2 Tone choose what to release. Its bands mixed Jamaican ska with punk, and most had Black and white members playing together on purpose. Bands could leave after one single, and Madness did.
blurb.adult: 2 Tone's structure was unusual: an artist-run imprint with major-label money and a contract that let acts leave after one single, which is why Madness's only 2 Tone record is its first. Its black-and-white graphic identity and integrated line-ups were a deliberate political statement, and its short life (1979 to 1986) tracks the Thatcher-era recession its biggest hit, 'Ghost Town', described.
